items.rootCause:
This is Android's own keyboard-focus highlight. It comes from how the test joins the room, not from app code. QA types the room code with `npm run adb -- type` (that is `adb shell input text`). Those injected key events have no FLAG_KEEP_TOUCH_MODE, so the window leaves touch mode (ViewRootImpl.checkForLeavingTouchModeAndConsume: a typing key calls ensureTouchMode(false)). The join then completes by itself on the sixth digit (CodeInput onComplete), so the joiner never touches the screen afterwards. Outside touch mode, Android gives input focus to the first focusable view of each new screen (ViewRootImpl.focusableViewAvailable / rootViewRequestFocus) and draws the default focus highlight over it. The first focusable view on the game screen is the 'me' card's accessible summary View (PlayerCard.tsx `accessible` → ReactViewManager.setAccessible → isFocusable = true). Why the evidence fits:
(1) The box's bounds are exactly that summary View, which covers the identity and score rows but not the status/buttons row (159×110 dp, ending above 'אין טעויות' and the flag button). That is where the box ends in fix14-RF8Y60PP2XZ-darkbox-p1joiner.png.
(2) The colour is the theme's colorControlHighlight over the background. 16% white over (15,18,24) gives exactly (54,56,61) on phone 1 (dark system theme). A light theme's ~12% black gives the one-level-darker box on phone 3.
(3) It is drawn content, not stale pixels, and needs no extra SurfaceFlinger layer.
(4) Any tap clears it: enterTouchMode clears focus from a view that is not focusableInTouchMode. The opponent's move does not.
(5) Never on the host, in ranked or in bot games: in those, the last input was a tap (start / search / play).
Real players on the on-screen keyboard stay in touch mode, because the IME keeps it and links are tapped, so they never see it. A hardware-keyboard user does see it, and there it is the correct focus indicator. I found no app state that differs for the joiner. Making the summary non-focusable would only move the box to the surrender button, and it would change how TalkBack groups the card. So there is no app change.

Its useSlam then started a spring from that point on its first frame. That first frame comes 120–140 ms later, because the new screen has to mount first. Meanwhile the room's own GO! (a separate spring) kept going, or stalled with the UI thread.
The screens are transparent and the room stays under the pushed game route for a few frames. For those 3–5 frames the cover's GO! (still at ~1.1–1.2) lay over the room's (at ~0.95–1). That was the 'bigger, doubled' GO!. It then slammed down again (a restart).
Measured from QA's zoom sheets (GO! bounding box per frame):
- off2-P3: the room's GO! held 65 px from 8200 to 8300, the doubled frames at 8320–8360 were 65 px, then 55 → 59 (dip and land).
- rm2: room 68 px, then the cover appeared at 81 px (≈1.2×) and slammed back to 67 px. So in that run the cover started from a point ~80 ms into the slam while GO! had been on screen ~220 ms.
Ranked does not jump because its cover is `still` (landed, at scale 1), the same as the match screen's held GO!.

The box is Android's own keyboard-focus highlight. QA's way of joining triggers it; the app code does not. QA types the room code with `npm run adb -- type`, which is `adb shell input text`. Those injected key events have no FLAG_KEEP_TOUCH_MODE, so the window leaves touch mode (ViewRootImpl.checkForLeavingTouchModeAndConsume calls ensureTouchMode(false) for a typing key). The join then completes by itself on the sixth digit (CodeInput onComplete), so the joiner never touches the screen afterwards.

Outside touch mode, Android gives input focus to the first focusable view of each new screen and draws the default focus highlight over it. On the game screen that view is the 'me' card's accessible summary View: PlayerCard `accessible` makes it focusable through ReactViewManager.setAccessible.

Why the evidence fits:
- The box has exactly that View's bounds (159×110 dp). It covers the identity and score rows and stops above the status/buttons row.
- The colour is the theme's colorControlHighlight over the background. 16% white over (15,18,24) gives exactly (54,56,61) on phone 1 (dark system theme). The light theme's ~12% black gives the one-level-darker box on phone 3.
- It is drawn content and has no SurfaceFlinger layer of its own.
- Any tap clears it: enterTouchMode drops focus from a view that is not focusableInTouchMode. The opponent's move does not clear it.
- It never shows on the host, in ranked or in bot games, because there the last input was a tap.

The lobby: QA saw no box there, although out of touch mode the lobby's first control is also focused. That control is a Pressable with a RippleDrawable, which reports its own focus state, so Android does not draw the default highlight on it.

I found no app state that differs for the joiner. Real players type on the on-screen keyboard, which keeps touch mode (and links are tapped), so they never see the box. A hardware-keyboard user does see it, and for them it is the correct focus indicator.

items.rootCause:
The game screen's GO! (GoCover → FriendsGoFrame → FriendsCountdown) took its point in the slam once, as the game screen rendered: sinceMs = now − shownAt. It then started a spring from that point on its own first frame. That frame comes 120–140 ms later, while the new route mounts. The room screen stays under the pushed game route for a few frames, so for 3–5 frames the cover's GO! (still at ~1.1–1.2) lay over the room's (at ~1). That is the 'bigger, doubled' GO!. The cover's GO! then slammed down again, which is the restart.

The reviewer's high issue said rm2 ran with the app in reduced motion. The QA sheet refutes that. I measured the GO! bounding box per 20 ms tile with pngjs in rec/f14-rm2-RF8Y30L038L-zoom.png:
- The room's own GO! was 96 px wide at 8160 (dim), 94 at 8180, 88 at 8200–8220, 83 at 8240–8260, 76 at 8280, 73 at 8300–8320, and 68 at 8340–8360. That is a full 1.41× → 1 slam, not a fade at a constant size, so the app was not reducing motion in rm2.
- That run set the system animations to 0. That does not switch the app's reduce on: useReduceMotion follows the app's own setting, which defaults to 'off' (spec §4.1), and follows the phone only when the setting is 'כמו במכשיר'.
- At 8400–8440 the box is 81 px with ~2690 yellow pixels. The single-layer 81 px frame at 8460 has 2174, so those frames are the union of two layers.
- After that: 75, 75, 70, 67, 67 px. That is the cover's GO! slamming again from 1.19 (81/68). 1.19 is the room's pose ~100–120 ms into its slam, which is 120–140 ms before the cover's first frame.

So rm2 confirms this root cause. With the app's own Reduce Motion on, the old code would also not have jumped: the cover was at scale 1.

The reviewer's medium issue was also real. My first version seeded the cover's GO! with the pose worked out at render time, and the view can be drawn before its UI-thread clock's first frame. That would have left the same wrong pose for one frame.

items.fix:
1) One clock for both GO!s, in apps/mobile/src/screens/game/connection/motion.ts. useSlamSince(reduce, origin) drives a shared value with withClockSince, a small defineAnimation. With Reduced Motion it is the fade only and the scale is always 1. useSlam lost its sinceMs parameter.

2) No stale first frame (the reviewer's medium issue). Until the clock's first UI frame, useSlamSince draws the slam's start (opacity 0), unless GO! had already landed by the render. items.rootCause: The pattern follows when the activity was created, not the screen. The app is edge-to-edge (RN 0.86, target 36). React Native picks the 3-button bar's scrim once per activity, in WindowUtil.kt enableEdgeToEdge (called from expo-modules-core's EdgeToEdgePackage activity listener): isAppearanceLightNavigationBars = !isDarkMode(activity), so a light scrim (0xE6FFFFFF, light grey, dark buttons) whenever the activity's configuration is not night. The app is dark (userInterfaceStyle 'dark'), but expo-system-ui applies that (AppCompatDelegate.setDefaultNightMode(MODE_NIGHT_YES)) in its own activity listener. That listener runs AFTER EdgeToEdgePackage's (ExpoModulesPackageList order: ...EdgeToEdgePackage, StatusBarPackage, SystemUIPackage). So an activity created first in its process (cold start or relaunch, as after adb.ts reset) on a phone in system light mode keeps a light bar for its whole life, on every screen. An activity recreated in the same process (the QA's density and font changes) finds night mode already set and gets the dark scrim. That is why the same screen differed between phones and between moments. No JS or per-screen call touches the navigation bar: there is only <StatusBar style="light"> in the root (and HelloScreen), and expo-navigation-bar is not installed. Modals' dialogs read the activity context's night mode the same way.

Instead, the standby mounts all opponents' avatars together (up to 3 in a 4-player game, about 40–130 nodes each), plus the ring and its EditText, in a single commit. On APK 20 one such avatar cost most of a 165–200 ms JS burst, and its mount (preMountItems, 14–30 ms per frame, over 3–5 frames) blocked HWUI frames. In a 4-player game that is likely up to about 3 times the old first-hit hitch. It falls in the first seconds of play, possibly under the player's first taps, and it is paid even if the player is never hit.
issues.evidence: HitLayer.tsx: bannerReady = useStandbyLater(kept.length > 0 ? 'banner' : null, …, HIT_BANNER_STANDBY_DELAY_MS), then a single <Banner … senders={kept} standby />. HitBanner.tsx maps every entry of `faces` to an <Avatar>. AvatarArt's StaticArt makes one SvgXml per instance, with staticXml markup for the 'wink' face; the opponents' cards draw the 'neutral' face, so that markup is not cached. The off1 trace shows the single hit avatar: 1 ClipPath, 1 Defs, about 120 Path/Circle, in the hit cluster at 194546.8–194547.1. The deviceCheck only asks for 'one cluster of about 140–260 views about 2.25–3.5 s after the board'. It checks neither the frame gaps nor the input latency around that cluster.
issues.suggestion: Mount one sender's avatar per idle moment: first the banner shell (ring, EditText, texts), then one avatar per whenIdle. Do not mount them all in one commit. Add to the deviceCheck: the longest main doFrame gap and RT DrawFrames gap around the standby cluster, compared with the same 2–4 s window on APK 20, and one cell tap timed inside that window, in a 4-player room.

issues.problem: HitRehearsal still runs its 'banner' step at 2.5 s, and it is now redundant. It mounts and then unmounts a second banner, with its own ring EditText and an avatar placeholder, about 250 ms after the standby banner, which already paid those native first-time costs and stays mounted. The result is wasted mount work in the same busy early-game window, and in about 0.25 s three warm-up events are packed together: the warp canvas at 2.0 s, the banner standby at 2.25 s, and the rehearsal at 2.5 s.
issues.evidence: HitRehearsal.tsx: rehearsalSteps() always starts with 'banner'. GameScreen.tsx still renders <HitRehearsal rules=… /> without changes. Its banner step mounts <HitBanner … /> at 1% opacity for HIT_REHEARSAL_HOLD_MS (250 ms).
issues.suggestion: Drop the 'banner' step from the rehearsal when the game has senders, so HitLayer's standby is the banner's warm-up. For example, pass a skipBanner flag, or compute the steps from whether hitSenders is non-empty.

issues.problem: When a hit ends early, the standby props are committed before the shared clock is reset. In that frame the banner can show at full opacity, empty: no title, no subtitle, no avatar, only the ring. This happens when hitBy is cleared, or `now` passes endsAt, while the UI-thread clock is still mid-hit, for example when the app comes back from the background after the hit ended, or when the server clears the hit early. issues.evidence: HitLayer.tsx, standby branch: <Banner title="" subtitle="" … elapsed={elapsed} standby />. issues.suggestion: Give the standby banner a clock that never moves (the layer already has `still = useSharedValue(0)` for the unseen effect). Pass elapsed={shown ? elapsed : still}. issues.problem: The standby's avatars are mounted whenever `senders` changes, including mid-hit. In ranked play, session.profiles can arrive after the game screen mounts. That changes `avatars`, so hitSendersOf, so `kept`. If it lands during a hit, the shown banner (senders={bannerReady ? kept : undefined}) mounts the new avatars under the hit. issues.evidence: GameScreen.tsx: the hitSenders useMemo depends on [view, avatars], and avatars depends on `profiles`. HitLayer.tsx useSameSenders: setKept(list) as soon as the key changes. The shown branch passes `kept` whenever bannerReady is true.
issues.suggestion: While a hit is on, hold the previous kept list; adopt a changed list only between hits, on an idle moment, through the same useStandbyLater gate. Otherwise, accept it as rare and note it in the comment.

items.rootCause:
What the APK 20 slices show. I grouped every createViewUnsafe in the six atrace files by time and type. The counts are the same in all six runs, sound on and off.

(1) Common to both conditions. The hit's own commit creates 141 native views (+0.40 to +0.89 s after the marker): 94 RNSVGPath, 21 RNSVGCircle, 6 RNSVGGroup, 3 RNSVGSvgView, 1 ClipPath, 1 Defs, 1 Ellipse, 2 Rect, 8 RCTView, 3 RCTText and 1 AndroidTextInput.
- There is exactly one ClipPath and one Defs, which means one whole avatar drawing was made from scratch. That is the sender's face in the hit banner: HitBanner was not mounted between hits.
- The banner accounts for about 130 of the 141 views: that avatar (about 120 SVG nodes), the ring's Svg, the ring's number (an animated read-only TextInput, an EditText that takes 8-18 ms to create on its own), and its texts and views.
- This explains the 165-200 ms JS burst, the 3-5 mount frames (preMountItems 14-30 ms each) and the 21-33 ms first Record View#draw, all inside the fade-in.

(2) A second mount 250-500 ms after the hit: 68 views (1 SvgView, 26 paths, 36 rects). This is my own card's avatar going into its dizzy and wobble layers (AVATAR_REACTIONS.on.hit). It lines up with the 110 ms stall in on2, together with the GC.

(3) Every warp, not only the first. The main thread draws the Skia overlay with GL itself: acquireBuffer, about 20 ms of untraced CPU, then eglSwapBuffers and queueBuffer on SurfaceTexture-0, waiting on Mali fences. That is the 25-47 ms 'animation' phase, and it holds the effect at about 30 fps.

(4) Sound ON only: CPU contention, nothing blocking. ExoPlayer rebuilds its AudioTrack on each play: only ExoPlayer:Audio and AudioTrack are new thread ids. doSomeWork takes 82-124 ms of wall time but only 36-45 ms of CPU. A NativeAlloc concurrent GC followed in 2 of 3 runs.

Ruled out by the traces: a blocking GC on main, shader or GL compile (10 ms or less), a long binder call, D state, an audio player created on main, and the volume setter.

Fixes cause (1). The hit banner is now made before the hit, during the existing standby after GO!, and spread over several idle moments.

First implementation (kept):
- hitModel.ts: HitSender, senderKeyOf() and hitSendersOf().
- GameScreen.tsx: passes hitSenders (null without interferences, D44) to HitLayer.
- HitBanner.tsx: new senders and standby props. Every kept sender's avatar sits in the avatar's place, and only the sender's is visible. In standby the banner is not accessible and hides its descendants.
- HitLayer.tsx: between hits the banner stays mounted, as the same memoised element, so a hit only changes its props.

Changes after the review:
- Medium (one big commit): fixed. At HIT_BANNER_STANDBY_DELAY_MS (2.25 s) plus an idle moment, only the bare banner is mounted (ring, text field, texts, no avatar). The new useWarmSenders adds one sender's avatar per HIT_BANNER_FACE_GAP_MS (250 ms) plus an idle moment. A 4-player game makes 4 small commits (about 2.25, 2.5, 2.75 and 3.0 s plus idle), never one with 3 avatars.
- Low (rehearsal): fixed. HitRehearsal has a new banner prop (default true), and rehearsalSteps(kinds, banner) leaves out the 'banner' step. GameScreen passes banner={!hitSenders?.length}, so a game that keeps a standby banner no longer mounts and unmounts a second banner at 2.5 s.
- Low (empty banner at full strength): fixed, a little differently from the reviewer's suggestion. The banner sits in one slot View whose static opacity is 0 whenever no hit is shown.   - I did not switch the standby to the `still` clock. That would recreate the banner's worklet at every hit (its closure changes), and a worklet registered in a passive effect could start the banner a frame after the dim, which is the APK 14 bug. Both branches still read the one hit clock.
- Low (senders changing mid-hit): fixed. useWarmSenders never changes its list while a hit is on. A list that changed during a hit (profiles that arrived late) is taken up after it, one avatar per idle moment. A sender who left is dropped between hits. Not changed, on purpose: (2) the avatar reaction (avatars area), (3) Skia's GL drawing on the UI thread (native, every warp), (4) the audio. No new strings. docs/design/motion.md: the hit.banner sentence is updated (LF).

The item is partial. The fix removes the first-hit cost shared by sound ON and OFF: the banner's ~130 native views, its JS render, its EditText and its first SVG build. Three costs remain:

(b) The target's avatar reaction at +250-500 ms: 68 views (avatars area, not touched).
(c) Sound ON: ExoPlayer rebuilds its AudioTrack on each play, and a NativeAlloc GC often follows. This is CPU contention and blocks nothing.

How each review issue was handled:
- Medium (all the avatars in one commit): fixed. The banner is mounted bare first, then one avatar every 250 ms plus an idle moment (useWarmSenders). The cost is +2 commits per game with 3 players (render bound 24 to 26). The deviceCheck now asks for frame gaps and tap latency in the 2-4 s window, in a 4-player room.

- Low (senders changing mid-hit): fixed. The list is frozen while a hit is on and taken up after it, one avatar per idle moment.

Not verified, needs the device: the standby keeps the avatars at opacity 0, and I expect Android to record their Record View#draw (RNSVG's software bitmap) on the UI thread even at alpha 0. Only the RT upload of a 34x34 bitmap would remain at the hit. The deviceCheck's 'no Record View#draw over 20 ms' step confirms this.

I made a temporary local mutation of HitLayer.tsx to confirm the new tests fail, then restored it from a scratchpad copy. There was no git write, adb, APK, deploy or npm install. The other hunk in motion.md (friends.countdown) belongs to another agent and was left as it is.
